qa.overall_assessment: Enter key sends messages correctly on web. Browser test confirmed: typed 'QA pipeline 3 test - enter key verification', pressed Enter, message appeared in chat (ref e833), input cleared, session status changed to 'divining...' indicating message was sent to server. MultiTextInput.web.tsx (the file used on web builds) has correct handleKeyDown with e.preventDefault() when Enter is handled. agentInputEnterToSend=true was verified in user settings.

checks.details: Lines 65-110: handleKeyDown maps Enter -> normalizedKey -> calls onKeyPress(keyEvent) -> if handled, calls e.preventDefault(). This fires before browser default behavior (React onKeyDown fires before textarea inserts characters).
Line 68: const isComposing = e.nativeEvent.isComposing || e.keyCode === 229; returns early if composing, preventing premature send during CJK input

checks.check: AgentInput.tsx handles Enter -> calls props.onSend() -> returns true
checks.details: Lines 531-538: agentInputEnterToSend && event.key === 'Enter' && !event.shiftKey && !isTouchDevice -> props.onSend() -> return true (triggers e.preventDefault in web.tsx)
localStorage 'mmkv.default\settings' shows agentInputEnterToSend: true in the test account settings
Line 530: const isTouchDevice = typeof window !== 'undefined' && ('ontouchstart' in window || navigator.maxTouchPoints > 0) - prevents Enter-to-send on touch devices

checks.check: Live browser test: Enter sends message
checks.details: Typed 'QA pipeline 3 test - enter key verification' in textbox ref e802. Pressed Enter. Snapshot immediately showed: message appeared in chat as ref e833, status changed to 'divining...', input cleared. URL remained on same session page (no navigation away).
evidence: qa-pipeline3-enter-sent.png - message visible in chat, input empty, divining... status

checks.details: Lines 122-137: useEffect attaches DOM-level keydown listener gated by Platform.OS === 'web'. On web builds, .web.tsx takes priority, so this listener is active only in native builds and non-web bundler contexts.

root_cause_verification.rationale: Root cause was submitBehavior='newline' causing textarea to insert newline before React's synthetic onKeyPress fired. Fix: MultiTextInput.web.tsx uses React's onKeyDown handler (fires before browser default) with e.preventDefault() when Enter is handled. Live test confirms messages send correctly on Enter key.

band_aid_detection.summary: No band-aid patterns. Fix addresses the correct event ordering issue at the DOM level.

regression_test_results.details: Code shows: if event.shiftKey -> normalizedKey is Enter but AgentInput only triggers send when !event.shiftKey, so Shift+Enter falls through to default textarea behavior (inserts newline)
